title: Real provider boundary justifies abstraction
task: Review whether a provider abstraction is justified for two production implementations with different SDKs and lifecycle behavior.
context: The service supports both Yandex and Edge TTS providers.
Callers should not depend on either provider SDK.
Provider-specific authentication, retry behavior, and capability metadata differ.
Both implementations are used in production.
evidence: Changing one provider SDK leaks into higher application layers.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Keep everything concrete because interfaces are overengineering.
Duplicate provider-specific logic in every caller.
Create one lowest-common-denominator interface that hides meaningful capability differences.
expected_decision_properties: Recognize a real provider boundary and recommend a stable abstraction.
Keep provider-specific behavior behind the provider boundary.
Avoid forcing materially different optional capabilities into false uniformity.
Prefer explicit capability discovery or scoped sub-interfaces when providers differ.
unacceptable_reasoning: All provider implementations must expose identical capabilities.
Any abstraction is unnecessary because two if-branches are simpler.
Provider SDK details should remain visible to callers for flexibility.
verification_expectations: Run provider contract tests for both implementations.
Verify provider-specific capability behavior remains explicit.
revisit_when: Provider capabilities converge enough to simplify the abstraction.
Only one provider remains and substitution is no longer required.
